Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

I will not attend the reception until I am asked to.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Unless.

Key Points​

  • The use of 'Until' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • Let us look at the meaning of the word "Unless and Until":
    • Unless: except if (used to introduce the case in which a statement being made is not true or valid).
    • Until: up to the point in time
  • Example:
    • Unless you have a photographic memory, repetition is vital.​
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Unless'.
     

​Correct sentence: I will not attend the reception unless I am asked to.

Additional Information

  • Though means despite the fact that; although.
    • Example:
      • Though they were speaking in undertones, Percival could hear them.
  • ​​Even means equal in number, amount, or value.
    • Except: not including; but not.
  • ​​Except means not including, but not.
    • Example:
      • They work every day except Sunday.

It is advisable that we should never impose to much work on anyone.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Too much.

Key Points​

  • The use of the phrase 'To much' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • The meaning of the phrase 'Too much' is an intolerable, impossible, or exhausting situation or experience.
  • Example:
    • The effort proved too much for her.
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Too much'.
     

​Correct sentence: It is advisable that we should never impose too much work on anyone.

Additional Information

  • 'Such' can be used as a determiner, predeterminer and pronoun which means of the type previously mentioned.
    • Example:
      • I have been involved in many such courses.
  • ​​'Very much' is an idiom which means to a very great degree or extent.
    • Example:
      • We enjoyed ourselves very much.
  • ​​'A lot' means many or to a great extent.
    • Example:
      • Mona reads a lot of books during her morning hours.

questions.text: According to the Prime Minister, what is dangerous and harmful to the development of the country?

options.text: The hindrance in the distribution of freebies.
The interference of Finance Commission in the distribution of freebies.
The less involvement of youth in distributing and accepting freebies.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'The distribution of freebies.'

Key Points

  • The given passage is all about the concern over ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.
  • The last sentence of the first paragraph says "He hit out at the Opposition parties for offering freebies and said that this was dangerous and harmful to the development of the country".
  • From the above sentences, we can say that according to the Prime Minister, the distribution of freebies is dangerous and harmful to the development of the country.
     

Hence, the only possible answer is option 2.

Important Points

  • ​Given below are the points, we should keep in mind while solving questions of reading comprehension-
    • Identify the purpose of reading. Try to go through the question first and then the passage so that you can just focus on the things you need to look at in the passage.
    • Anticipate what may lie ahead. Look out for specific information in the passage.

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are incorrect according to the given passage?

A. Mr. Narendra Modi warned the youth not to get carried away by freebies.

B. The Court has suggested the Finance Commission to stay out of the matter of the 'freebies' issue.

C. The Chief Justice of India remarked ‘freebies’ as an unimportant issue.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both B and C.'

Key Points

  • The second sentence of the first paragraph says "Speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the Bundelkhand Expressway (Uttar Pradesh) on July 16, Prime Minister Narendra Modi warned youth not to get carried away by the ‘revari culture’, where votes are sought by promising ‘freebies’.''
    • From the above sentence, we can say that statement A is correct according to the given passage.​​​
  • The last sentence of the second paragraph says "The Court also suggested that the Finance Commission could be involved to look into the matter and propose solutions'' and the second sentence of the second paragraph says "It has been reported that during the hearing, the Chief Justice of India remarked that ‘freebies’ were a serious issue and asked the Central government to take a stand on the need to control the announcement of ‘freebies’ by political parties during election campaigns''.
    • From the above sentence, we can say that statements B and C are incorrect according to the given passage.​
       

Hence, the only possible answer is option 4.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of the word 'Distort'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Accurate.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Distort' means To give a misleading or false account or impression of something.
    • Example: They said that it had printed false information to distort the facts.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Accurate​ - Correct in all details; exact.
      • Example: She gave an accurate account of the case.
    • Pervert - To distort or corrupt the original course, meaning, or state of something.
      • Example: He was charged with conspiring to pervert the course of justice.
    • Garble - To reproduce something in a confused and distorted way.
      • Example: You garble my words from their real meaning.
    • Prejudice - Preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.
      • Example: The party's policies were based on prejudice rather than on any coherent ideology.
    • Misrepresent - To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.
      • Example: These statistics grossly misrepresent the reality.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • The antonyms of the word 'Distort' are "Accurate, Interpret, Decipher".
  • The synonyms of the word 'Distort' are "Pervert​, Garble, Misrepresent".

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Irrational'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Fallacious.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Irrational' means Not logical or reasonable.
    • Example: She has an irrational dread of hospitals.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Logical - Characterized by or capable of clear, sound reasoning.
      • Example: Students need the ability to construct a logical argument.
    • Reasonable - Having sound judgment; fair and sensible.
      • Example: It seems a perfectly reasonable request to make.
    • Sound - Based on valid reason or good judgement.
      • Example: She gave me some very sound advice.
    • Valid - Having a sound basis in logic or fact; reasonable or cogent.
      • Example: Accepting valid criticism is also part of this group of assertive actions.
    • Fallacious - Based on a false idea; illogical.
      • Example: His argument is based on fallacious reasoning.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 5.

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word 'Irrational' are "Fallacious, Illogical, Invalid".
  • The antonyms of the word 'Irrational' are "Logical, Reasonable, Valid".

In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column, phrases are A, B, and C, and in the second column, the phrases are D, E and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer.  

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) The trend continues to this day and has spread to 

(D) respect for the whole community.

(B) Our love for the country should be conditioned by

(E) our duties and responsibilities towards that family.

(C) We are the members of a large human family and so cannot neglect 

(F) recently industrialized portions of the world.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e., A-F, B-D and C-E.

Key PointsWe need to join the sentence segments in column 1 with those in column 2 to create sentences that are conceptually and grammatically correct. Let us see how the sentence parts can join.

  • Part A talks about the spread of a certain trend, so conceptually, it should join with the part that explains where the trend has spread to. So, A-F. 
  • Part B talks about a conditioning and the use of the preposition 'by' means it should be followed by the part that acts as the agent of this 'conditioning'. Between, parts D and E, part D is a better fit (part E talks about 'family' which is not relevant here). So, B-D.
  • Part C talks about 'we' being a part of a family and how 'we' cannot neglect something. Part E best mentions what 'we' cannot neglect. So, C-D.
     

In the given options, all three joined sentences are reflected in option 3, making it the correct answer.

Key PointsWe need to join the sentence segments in column 1 with those in column 2 to create sentences that are conceptually and grammatically correct. Let us see how the sentence parts can join.

  • Part A talks about books and ends with the coordinating conjunction 'but'. Contextually, it best joins with part F as it deals with 'reading'. Grammatically, this joining is correct as 'but' joins two clauses that are equal in importance but contrast with each other. So, A-F.
  • Part B states how prejudice brings nothing. It cannot be joined with part D as it talks about rainfall. Joining it to part E is also grammatically and contextually incorrect. So, part B and part E are incomplete sentence segments.

Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. if the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any.

He's living (A) with luxury (B) in the south (C) of France. (D) No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • The error lies in Part B of the sentence. 
  • Use 'in' in place of 'with'.
  • In - used to indicate inclusion within something abstract or immaterial.
    • Ex: He was sitting alone in the darkness.
  • With- We use with to refer to what we use to do something.
    • Ex: They opened the package with a knife.
  • Therefore, by understanding the usage of the above preposition it is clear that 'in' is the correct answer.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
     

The correct sentence is: He's living in luxury in the south of France.

The correct sentence: I always play cricket in the morning. But last morning I played baseball.
 Important Points

Directions: In the following questions, a sentence is given with five words marked as (A), (B), (C), (D) & (E). These words may or may not be placed in their places. Four options with different arrangements of these words are given. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If there is no change required, mark ‘No rearrangement required’ as your answer.

Roger Federer and Serena Williams, both of whom will turn 40 in 2021, have already players (A) to allowed (B) in Australia but the committed (C) simply will not show up if they are not playing (D) to prepare (E) properly.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is CDABE.

Important Points

Let us consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first, B the second, and so on.
  • The first blank requires a past participle as it is preceded by the verb 'have'. Thus, the correct answer is 'committed'. 
  • The second blank requires a verb in the present continuous tense and 'allowed' is in the past tense, thus the correct answer is 'playing'. 
  • The third blank requires a noun, as a verb is not an entity that can 'show up'. Thus, the correct answer is 'players'. 
  • The fourth blank requires a verb in the past tense, thus the correct answer is 'allowed'. 
  • The fifth blank requires a verb in the present tense, thus the correct answer is 'prepare'. 'To' is usually followed by the base form of the verb.

Additional Information

Let's look at the meaning of the words:

  • Committed: Past tense of 'commit', which means to be dedicated to something, to agree to do something. 
  • Playing: Present continuous tense of 'play', which means to take part in a sport. 
  • Players: Plural of 'player', which is a person who is taking part in a sport or a game.
  • Allowed: Past tense of 'allow', which means to give permission to someone; agreeing to let them do something.
  • Prepare: Make something ready for use; to become ready to perform. 
     

Thus, the correct sentence: Roger Federer and Serena Williams, both of whom will turn 40 in 2021, have already committed to playing in Australia but the players simply will not show up if they are not allowed to prepare properly.

Over the past week, population (A) in Hyderabad have pressure (B) 33 people and floods (C) property; authorities blame the inflating killed (D) and rapid infrastructural development which have put a tremendous destroyed (E) on the water bodies of the city.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is CDEAB.

Important Points

Let us consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first, B the second and so on.
  • The first blank requires a noun that can have a tangible effect on something, something that can directly cause deaths and destruction. Thus, 'population' is incorrect, and 'floods' is correct. 
  • Since the 2nd blank is preceded by the helping verb 'have', a past participle must be used here. 'Have/has + past participle' forms present perfect tense. Thus the correct answer is 'killed'. 
  • The third blank requires a verb in the past tense as it is an action that is happening to property in Hyderabad. Thus, the correct answer is 'destroyed'. 
  • The fourth blank requires a noun that can be preceded by the adjective 'inflating', thus the correct answer is 'population'. 
  • The fifth blank requires a noun that can be preceded by an adjective 'tremendous'. Thus, the correct answer is 'pressure'. 

Additional Information

Let's look at the meaning of the words:

  • Floods: The overflow of large amounts of water beyond its normal limits.
  • Killed: Died; was dead due to some cause. 
  • Destroyed: Ruined or damaged something.
  • Population: The inhabitants of a particular place. 
  • Pressure: Continuous physical force put o or against someone or something. 
     

Thus, the correct sentence is: Over the past week, floods in Hyderabad have killed 33 people and destroyed property; authorities blame the inflating population and rapid infrastructural development which have put a tremendous pressure on the water bodies of the city.

The modified (A) of the two Boeing 777 aircrafts (B) extensively second (C) for the President, the Vice President and Prime Minister’s arrive (D) will travel (E) in national capital Delhi on Saturday.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is CBAED.

Important Points

Let us consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first, B the second and so on.
  • The first blank requires a proper noun, something specific that is being referred to and thus cannot be a verb like 'modified'. Thus, the correct answer is 'second'. 
  • The second blank requires a noun that the preceding label 'Boeing 777' is a category of, and 'Boeing 777' is a type of aircraft and so 'aircrafts' is the correct answer. 
  • The third blank requires a verb in the past tense and thus an adjective like 'second' needs to be replaced with the verb 'modified'. 
  • The fourth blank requires a noun and 'arrive' is a verb, thus the correct answer is 'travel'. 
  • The fifth blank requires a verb in the present tense (infinitive form) and one cannot 'travel in' a location, one can 'travel to' a location, thus the correct answer is 'arrive'. 

Additional Information  

Let' look at the meaning of all the words:

  • Second: Refers to the number 2 in the sequence; the next in line. 
  • Aircraft: An aeroplane, a helicopter or a machine capable of flying. 
  • Modified: Past tense of 'modify' which means to make changes to or in. 
  • Travel: The act of travelling. 
  • Arrive: To reach the place at the end of a journey; the final stage of a journey. 

Thus, the correct sentence will be: The second of the two Boeing 777 aircrafts extensively modified for the President, the Vice President and Prime Minister’s travel will arrive in national capital Delhi on Saturday.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is BAEDC.

Key Points 

  • Let us consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first, B the second and so on.
  • The first blank requires a noun that refers to a living thing as it makes the action of 'casting' something, which can only be done by living things and a 'ballot' is a non-living thing. Thus the correct answer is 'astronaut'. 
  • The second blank requires a non-living noun as only a non-living thing can be 'cast', thus the correct answer is 'ballot'. 
  • The third blank requires a non-proper noun as there is only one 'Earth' (that we know of) and so it does not belong to any particular person, so it cannot be preceded by a possessive pronoun like 'her'. Thus, the correct answer is 'voice'.
  • The fourth blank is preceded by the adjective 'presidential' which refers to something related to the president, and of the available options, 'election' is the most appropriate answer. 
  • The fifth blank requires a proper noun as it is preceded by the article 'the' which is used to refer to proper nouns, thus the correct answer is 'Earth'. 

Additional Information 

Let's look at the meaning of all the words:

  • Astronaut: A person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft
  • Ballot: A system of voting secretly and writing on a particular issue
  • Voice: A particular opinion or attitude that a person has towards something. 
  • Election: A formal and organized choice by vote if a person for a political office. 
  • Earth: The planet on which we live; the world. 
     

So, the correct sentence would be- A US astronaut cast her ballot from the International Space Station on Thursday, making her voice heard in the presidential election despite being 408km above the Earth.

questions.text: A man drives from Bhopal to Agra without taking rest. It covers first 150 km at the speed of 75 km/h. What is the car’s average speed for the remaining 130 km. If overall average speed in the entire journey is 70 km/h?

Remaining distance = 130

Overall average speed in entire journey = 70 km

Concept used:

Average speed = (Total distance)/(Total time)

Calculations:

Time taken in first 150 km = 150/75 = 2 hr

Total distance = 150 + 130 = 280 km

So, total time = Distance/Speed

⇒ 280/70 = 4 hrs

Time for rest of the journey = 4 – 2 = 2 hrs

Average speed for the remaining journey = 130/2 = 65 km/hr

∴ The car’s average speed for the remaining journey is 65 km/h

Into a cylindrical tank filled with a certain amount of water 88 iron blocks were dropped. Due to this water in the tank rose by 4 mm. find the weight of the iron blocks dropped if the diameter of the tank is 14 m and each block weighs the same.

The volume of water rose = sum of the weight of 88 iron blocks

⇒ weight of 1 iron block = 616/88 Kg

⇒ weight of 1 iron block = 7 Kg

∴ Weight of each iron block is 7 kg.

questions.text: In which of the following coupling, one module can modify the data of another module or control flow is passed from one module to the other module?
questions.explanation:
Data Coupling: If the dependency between the modules is based on the fact that they communicate by passing only data, then the modules are said to be data coupled. In data coupling, the components are independent to each other and communicating through data. Module communications don’t contain tramp data. Example-customer billing system.

Stamp Coupling: In stamp coupling, the complete data structure is passed from one module to another module. Therefore, it involves tramp data. It may be necessary due to efficiency factors- this choice made by the insightful designer, not a lazy programmer.

Control Coupling: If the modules communicate by passing control information, then they are said to be control coupled. It can be bad if parameters indicate completely different behavior and good if parameters allow factoring and reuse of functionality. Example- sort function that takes comparison function as an argument.

External Coupling: In external coupling, the modules depend on other modules, external to the software being developed or to a particular type of hardware. Ex- protocol, external file, device format, etc.

Common Coupling: The modules have shared data such as global data structures. The changes in global data mean tracing back to all modules which access that data to evaluate the effect of the change. So it has got disadvantages like difficulty in reusing modules, reduced ability to control data accesses and reduced maintainability.

Content Coupling: In a content coupling, one module can modify the data of another module or control flow is passed from one module to the other module. This is the worst form of coupling and should be avoided.

questions.text: Which concurrency control technique uses locks to manage data access?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Two-phase locking(2PL).

Key Points

  • Two-phase locking (2PL) is a concurrency control method used in database systems.
  • It ensures serializability by dividing the lock acquisition and release into two distinct phases.
  • The two phases are growing phase (locks are acquired but not released) and shrinking phase (locks are released but not acquired).
  • By following this protocol, 2PL avoids conflicts and ensures consistent transaction execution.
  • It is a widely used approach in database management systems for concurrency control.

Additional Information

  • Timestamp Ordering:
    • This technique uses timestamps to order transactions and ensure serializability.
    • Each transaction is assigned a unique timestamp to manage access conflicts.
  • Optimistic Concurrency Control:
    • This method assumes minimal conflicts and validates transactions during the commit phase.
    • It is often used in scenarios where conflicts are rare.
  • Multiversion Concurrency:
    • This technique maintains multiple versions of data for concurrent access.
    • It allows readers to access older versions while writers update the data.
  • Snapshot Isolation:
    • This ensures that transactions see a consistent snapshot of the database at a specific point in time.
    • It helps avoid conflicts by isolating transaction views.

questions.text: Which of the following algorithms solves the all-pairs shortest path problem?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Floyd's algorithm

Key Points

  • Dijkstra's Algorithm: ❌ Dijkstra's algorithm is primarily used to find the shortest path from a single source to all vertices in a graph. It does not solve the all-pairs shortest path problem.
  • Floyd's Algorithm: ✅ Floyd-Warshall algorithm is specifically designed to solve the all-pairs shortest path problem. It works by iteratively improving the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices using a dynamic programming approach.
  • Prim's Algorithm: ❌ Prim's algorithm is used for finding the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a graph, not for solving shortest path problems.
  • Warshall's Algorithm: ❌ Warshall's algorithm is used for transitive closure of a graph, not for solving the all-pairs shortest path problem.

Additional Information

  • The Floyd-Warshall algorithm is a dynamic programming algorithm that compares all possible paths between every pair of vertices in a weighted graph to find the shortest paths.
  • It has a time complexity of O(V³), where V is the number of vertices in the graph.
  • This algorithm works for both directed and undirected graphs, as long as there are no negative weight cycles in the graph.
  • The main advantage of Floyd-Warshall is its simplicity and ability to handle dense graphs efficiently.

questions.text: Why does Boyce–Codd Normal Form (BCNF) impose stricter conditions than Third Normal Form?

options.text: BCNF requires every determinant to be a candidate key

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is BCNF requires every determinant to be a candidate key(Option 3).

Key Points

  • Boyce–Codd Normal Form (BCNF) imposes stricter conditions than Third Normal Form.
  • BCNF is a higher form of normalization in relational database design.
  • BCNF addresses anomalies that can arise due to dependencies in 3NF.
  • It requires that every determinant in the relation must be a candidate key.
  • This ensures that no redundancy or anomalies occur in the database design.
  • BCNF eliminates situations where non-prime attributes depend on non-candidate key attributes.
  • It supports lossless decomposition and preserves dependencies.

Additional Information

  • Third Normal Form (3NF):
    • Ensures that all attributes are dependent only on the primary key.
    • It allows transitive dependencies under certain conditions.
  • Multivalued Dependencies:
    • These occur when one attribute in a relation depends on another attribute in multiple ways.
    • BCNF does not directly address multivalued dependencies; they are tackled in Fourth Normal Form.
  • Join Dependencies:
    • BCNF does not eliminate join dependencies, as they are handled in Fifth Normal Form.
    • Join dependencies arise when relations need to be decomposed to avoid redundancy.
